targets.old_statement: Red-flashing responders command pull-over stops while blue, green and amber displayers earn only courtesy, and Move Over separately protects every stopped shoulder vehicle regardless of lights.
targets.old_spoken_statement: Red-flashing responders command pull-over stops while blue, green and amber displayers earn only courtesy, and Move Over separately protects every stopped shoulder vehicle regardless of lights.
targets.statement: Authorized emergency vehicles flashing red, red-and-blue, or red-and-white lights require pulling safely to the right edge and stopping, whereas vehicles displaying only blue, green, or amber lights receive courtesy yielding, and the Move Over law requires slowing—and changing lanes when safe on multilane controlled-access roads—for stopped lit emergency or hazard vehicles and for any stopped motor vehicle on a parkway or controlled-access highway.

targets.old_statement: U-turns demand leftmost staging with green-arrow permission and long sight lines, yet die outright on expressways, in school zones, in city business districts and at posted signs.
targets.old_spoken_statement: U-turns demand leftmost staging with green-arrow permission and long sight lines, yet die outright on expressways, in school zones, in city business districts and at posted signs.
targets.statement: Allowed U-turns start only from the left portion of the lane nearest the centerline—including on a green left-turn arrow where permitted while yielding—and require five-hundred-foot visibility both ways, whereas U-turns are barred outright on limited-access expressways, in school zones, in New York City business districts, and at NO U-TURN signs.

targets.old_statement: Three-point turns choreograph right-stop, left-sweep, right-back and left-exit in that fixed order, the only maneuver in the chapter with a numbered script.
targets.old_spoken_statement: Three-point turns choreograph right-stop, left-sweep, right-back and left-exit in that fixed order, the only maneuver in the chapter with a numbered script.
targets.statement: A three-point turn follows four ordered steps: signal right and stop at the right edge; signal left, check traffic, and turn left across the road to stop facing the left curb; check traffic, turn the wheel fully right, and back up stopping short of the right curb; then check traffic, turn fully left, and pull forward when safe.
